text:
mike: Heads-up — cloud notified us of a list-price change for H100 in us-west1 and europe-west4, effective next billing cycle. This will impact our committed capacity math for Dedicated and private on-prem cloud pass-through. Need a quick margin check.

anya: Ugh. Do we have the exact numbers? Is it across all SKUs or just H100?

billing-bot: Invoice alert: projected monthly spend increase +$24,000 on GPU compute (estimated). See /billing/price-change-1782 for details.

mike: From vendor note: H100 on-demand goes from $3.00/hr -> $3.75/hr in us-west1 (25%). Reserved/committed discounts may still apply but vendor expects list prices to set baseline for new commits.

vincent: That 25% delta sounds like it could creep into our unit economics if we don't re-price or renegotiate. Quick back-of-envelope:
```
old_gpu_hr = $3.00
new_gpu_hr = $3.75
delta = $0.75/hr (25%)
fleet_monthly_hours = 32,000
monthly_delta = 0.75 * 32,000 = $24,000
```

sara: Thanks — that's the billing-bot number. For Hosted API today our infra cost per 1M tokens is roughly $X (see internal sheet). If infra cost goes +25% our blended unit cost increases ~ +8% after amortization across model mix.

elaine: Finance note: current gross margin target for Hosted API is 48%. If we absorb the $24k/month without price changes, margin drops ~1.2 percentage points. If we pass entire cost to customers, pricing elasticity unknown.

ops-kyra: On the Dedicated side customers on committed contracts have fixed pricing for 12/24mo windows. This mostly affects new commits and renewals. We should model a scenario where new committed asks increase price by 10-15% to keep margin.

anya: Two asks: (1) short-term: can we absorb the delta for next 2 months while we run negotiation? (2) medium-term: what's the impact on our Reserved offering pricing tiers and sales collateral?

mike: For (1) operations can smooth via shifting some non-critical workloads to lower-cost regions and tighten autoscale thresholds. We have ~4k GPU hours/mo in europe-west1 spare that are cheaper. But cross-region data egress and latency concerns for Dedicated customers.

vincent: Also consider temporary burst credit from vendor — we have a rep but need a good-faith forecast to negotiate. If we commit to X hours/mo for 12 months they might offer blended $/hr closer to old list.

elaine: I'll run sensitivity in the revenue model. Need: current committed revenue by account, renewal window schedule, and blended infra hours by model. Can ops export per-customer GPU-hour consumption for last 3 months?

ops-kyra: Yes — exporting now. ETA 90m. Will include per-region, per-model, and per-customer breakdown.

mike: Quick mitigation options from infra: 1) Delay low-priority batching jobs to off-peak in cheaper regions. 2) Increase KV prefix cache for popular requests to cut token compute. 3) Switch some models to quantized variants where latency allows (saves ~20% GPU time).

sara: Note on packaging: if we raise prices on new Dedicated commits, we can offer a "price-protection addendum" for existing customers as an upsell and limit churn. Suggest tiered: 6mo protected at +5%, 12mo at +8%.

anya: Good idea. Also update Sales playbook to include "cloud pass-through" clause for future contracts so list price hikes are transparent. Legal needs to review.

elaine: I'll produce 3 scenarios by EOD: (A) absorb for 3 months, (B) pass through 50% to customers, (C) full pass-through + increase new commit pricing. Each will show margin delta and churn risk estimate.

vincent: Add a 4th scenario: renegotiate with vendor for a 12-mo commit at blended rate to cap unit cost. Compare blended hourly to current and show break-even commit size.

mike: Practical ask to ops: after you export, can you run a quick script to compute our per-customer incremental margin impact if infra cost rises 25%? One-table output is fine.

ops-kyra: On it. Will run delta per-customer and a top-10 list of customers by sensitivity.

billing-bot: FYI — support ticket opened with vendor (TKT-4321) requesting pricing stabilization options.

sara: Also flag product: if we reduce model quality or swap quantized variants for cost, product needs to approve regressions and update evals. @product please weigh in.

mike: I'll sync with Sales for messaging. @elaine once you have scenarios, let's set a 30min review with GTM & Product.

elaine: Will do. Target 4:00pm PT.

anya: Thanks team — prioritize the export and the vendor negotiation. Emoji :thumbsup:

mike: Closing loop: short-term ops mitigations + finance scenarios + vendor negotiation. Keep thread updated.
